statement: Let X be smooth projective and rationally connected, let L = −KX be smoothly semipositive, and let an algebraic torus T act with the natural linearization. Let π : Z → X, g : Z → Y resolve a dominant invariant rational map, with Y smooth projective of positive dimension and C(Y ) relatively algebraically closed in C(X). Write E = KZ/X. Suppose a nonzero invariant rational section s of ℓπ∗L, ℓ > 0, and rational divisors N on Y and D on Z satisfy ℓ−1 divZ(s) = g∗ N + D, D ≥ 0. Assume that N has a semipositive metric with locally bounded weights. Suppose there is a rational simple normal crossings divisor ∆ = ∆+ − ∆− on Y , with every coefficient of ∆+ less than one, such that −KY − ∆ is nef. Let B be a reduced effective divisor on Y such that (i) Supp ∆− ⊂ Supp B; (ii) π∗(D − tg∗B) ≥ 0 for every sufficiently small rational t > 0; (iii) above every base prime outside B, some prime dominating it has coefficient zero in both D and E. Finally suppose the invariant generic spaces of E + kπ∗L have rank one for k = 0 and every positive multiple of one fixed integer. Then either H0(X, rL)T ̸= 0 for some r > 0, or a rational map Y 99K Y ′ with dim Y ′ < dim Y gives a composite fibration retaining a nonzero invariant generic section in a positive multiple of L and invariant adjoint rank one at zero and in every sufficiently divisible positive degree.
